findings.description: F-016: the uppercase-constant convention was attributed to chapter 13, which never teaches it; no chapter 1-16 does, so this was also a small prerequisite gap.
findings.resolution: Replaced the false cross-reference in build_16() with an in-place explanation: the name is uppercase because that is how Python code names module constants (a PEP 8 convention between programmers, not an interpreter-enforced restriction). Chapter HTML rebuilt.

find_winner(board) returns (mark, (a,b,c)) for a completed line and (None, None) otherwise. -- confirmed exhaustively -- for each of the 8 lines and each of X and O, find_winner returns exactly that mark and tuple (16/16); empty and partial boards return (None, None).

find_winner knows nothing about Tkinter and takes a plain list of strings, which is what makes it testable without a window. -- confirmed -- imported tic_tac_toe and called find_winner on plain lists with no tk.Tk() in existence at all.
